topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course context, her background, and the learning objectives regarding environmental exposures and cancer development.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Genetics, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer development, exploring the interaction between endogenous mutation rates, genetic predisposition, and environmental risk factors across populations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents and chronic infections contribute to cancer development, illustrated through the mechanism of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and DNA Damage Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific dietary, environmental, and chemical agents undergo metabolic activation to induce direct DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, including the role of chronic inflammation, chemical promoters, and host developmental windows in facilitating tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify and validate carcinogenic agents.

topics.label: Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes with a summary of cancer causality and the everyday decisions involved in weighing carcinogen exposure against practical benefits.
